request: explain the OSI model of networking

composition.story: Packets flow down through the seven layers of the OSI model during transmission and back up during reception. Each layer adds or removes specific encapsulation.

aha.observation: Layer 4 divides data into segments, establishing reliable end-to-end communication before routing.

states.label: 7. Application
states.sentence: The application layer interfaces directly with software applications.
states.why: Provides network services to user applications.

states.label: 6. Presentation
states.sentence: Data is translated, encrypted, and compressed here.
states.why: Ensures data is in a readable format for the application layer.

states.label: 5. Session
states.sentence: Manages communication sessions and dialogs between hosts.
states.why: Controls opening, closing, and establishing connections.

states.label: 4. Transport
states.sentence: Segments data and guarantees reliable delivery using TCP or UDP.
states.why: Handles error checking and flow control end-to-end.

states.label: 3. Network
states.sentence: Adds logical IP addresses and handles packet routing.
states.why: Determines the best path across interconnected networks.

states.label: 2. Data Link
states.sentence: Frames packets and uses MAC addresses for node-to-node delivery.
states.why: Manages physical media access and error detection on the local link.

states.label: 1. Physical
states.sentence: Transmits raw binary bits over physical network media.
states.why: Converts frames into electrical, optical, or radio signals.
